title: Game SFX?
author: EchoingAngel
selftext:
I've tried Eleven Labs and it has gone very poorly for making a single semi-unique sound. I spent the entire free 10k credits at 80-120 per run of 4 attempts with only 2 clips similar, but far from good enough. I tried describing the sound in dozens of different ways and even using their little refinements sometimes.

Are there any AI tools that are actually good at SFX, or are there any good purchasable SFX bundles out right now? (for commercial use)

comments.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
comments.body:
There are loads of good sound fx bundles but I can’t point to any because I’m personally making my own fx which is kind of easy because retro sounds. 

Anyways I don’t think ai would be super helpful for making sounds, probably helpful for searching for bundles though.

Little tip, sometimes letting sound fx really works well… also will make them unique to your project. Unlikely people will layer 2-4 sounds the same way you will.

replies.author: EchoingAngel
replies.body: The imagined sound of releasing giant clouds of gas/dust with a "strong" upfront sound and drawn out follow-through. It's something that is rather abstract, as it isn't a "real" sound (at least not very audible)

replies.author: Exhales_Deeply
replies.body: try thwump, fwump, fwoosh. fireball will also get close just none with crackle, and roll off the high end so you're just getting that big bassy fwoooom

replies.author: CycleMother2006
replies.body: You can always use a sound editor to tweak existing sounds to get the exact variation you're looking for. AI can even help with that. Probably easier than trying to make a sound from scratch if you have such constraints. There are sfx generators out there but you generally won't get anything particularly better than the free stuff and you'll probably still have to edit your sounds for equalization and stuff so they're not all over the place regardless.

comments.author: devtainer
comments.body:
I know what exactly are you talking about as I went through it. Here are my latest findings:
- eleven labs do sucks at sound generation. The only more less acceptable AI generation I found at the moment - codex, was using astra with it.
- still wont make you good sounds, so what I did - I've set up a skill for it to try fisrt find free sounds on available soursec (e.g. freesound) and preview it to me. So it decudes when it it easier to find it or when it is easier to generate
- still not works perfectly and sometimes get stuck at a simple thing, so I could search for sounds my self and give codex to process it(cuts, combinations, pitching etc)
- buy sound packs and let llm search through it as well
- what really helps is when you are not describing to llm what is sound for, but rather tell it what it should sound like. For exaple: i needed a sound for ice crystal blowing an aoe freezing attack. If you tell this to llm it will give you some crap. But then I thought about sound itself, it should be something like a wind raising-peak-falling down, which could be easily imagined by a big object on a high speed getting close, passing by and then fly away. So on the last explanation it finally started to give me what I wanted. So it is still some artwork by the end, you need to imagine things very clear.

So that's it.
